Hi Jackson —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and next steps from our side on HIPAA/BAA and where Redwood can fit in for MedWise: 

1) BAA availability: Redwood does offer a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement for customers handling PHI. We have a standard BAA that covers our hosted (Redwood API) and Dedicated modes; for on-prem / fully air-gapped Private deployments, customers often pair a Private control plane with their own KMS and Redwood legal works from the standard BAA as a starting point.

2) PHI handling boundaries: for hosted API (shared tenants) we require contract-level controls and design constraints — Redwood does not perform any PHI processing unless a BAA is executed and the customer selects an eligible deployment mode. Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools) and Private (VPC/on-prem) are the recommended modes for PHI workloads. We also provide token-level logging controls and options to disable retention.

3) Eligible deployment modes:
   - Hosted API (eligible with signed BAA + attestation; we recommend Dedicated for production PHI)
   - Dedicated (recommended for predictable throughput + isolation)
   - Private (VPC or on-prem) for strict regulatory controls and air-gapped needs

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll attach our draft BAA + a short deployment matrix.
- David (cc) will follow up with a brief note on technical boundaries and our recommended network controls.
- Could you share MedWise’s vendor security questionnaire and any specific retention/KMS requirements?

If that sounds right, I’ll kick off legal and security for a BAA draft and share a timeline (usually 7–10 business days to review).

Thanks,

Jackson — quick technical notes following Marissa's summary: 

- For PHI we recommend either Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives you customer-isolated GPU pools and network segregation inside our managed environment. Private gives you full control over networking and KMS; it can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem.
- Logging: we can configure token-level masking and opt-out of persistent logs for requests that contain PHI. By default we retain short-term logs for debugging; retention window is configurable under contract.
- Encryption: data at rest and in transit are encrypted; for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys (CMK) in supported clouds; Private supports HSM/KMS integrations per customer policy.
- Integration considerations: if you plan to use streaming or long context windows, we should validate KV cache handling and whether PHI appears in system prompts — those are operational constraints rather than technical blockers.

Happy to set up a short tech deep-dive with your security/infra folks to walk through network diagrams and key rotation.

Cheers,
David Kim
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Jackson — appreciate the questions. Quick answers and proposed path: 

1) Hosted API (shared) + BAA: Our standard stance is that hosted/shared may be eligible for BAA in limited scenarios if the customer accepts additional contractual and operational constraints (e.g., strict retention settings, low-volume, no third-party integrations that cache PHI). For most production PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private. We can enumerate the exact constraints in the BAA addendum.

2) Data deletion & logs: We provide contract-level guarantees for log retention windows and can disable persistent request/response logging for specific routes. We also support on-demand manual purge requests and can document the SLA for purges in the contract.

3) Vendor questionnaire: Thanks — we can take the first pass to fill out the sections we maintain (infrastructure, encryption, incident response). It would be great if you can answer any MedWise-specific policy/QoS questions after that. I’ll attach our filled copy once done.

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll route the MedWise questionnaire to our security team and return a filled PDF within 2 business days.
- Legal will prepare the BAA draft (I attached our standard template). We’ll flag any deployment-specific addenda for Dedicated vs Private.
- David to schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive next week with MedWise infra/security to validate network diagrams and KMS needs.

If you’re good with that timeline, I’ll kick everything off today.
